lesson.title: Limit data and cybersecurity presumptions
lesson.summary: Limit data and cybersecurity claims to their conditions and scope.

prerequisites.reason: The data presumption must be limited to its particular requirement. A cybersecurity certificate must be evaluated as a limited presumption.

blocks: Article 42(1)'s **contextual data presumption** concerns relevant Article 10(4) requirements for systems trained and tested on data reflecting the intended geographical, behavioural, contextual or functional setting. It does not presume every data-governance or system requirement satisfied. Data from another setting needs an evidence-based relevance check.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 42(1)–(3); CRA Articles 2 and 12

blocks: Article 42(2)'s **cybersecurity presumption** requires a certificate or statement under a Regulation 2019/881 cybersecurity scheme whose references are published in the Official Journal. It extends only as far as that evidence covers Article 15 cybersecurity requirements. It is not a presumption about accuracy, robustness or every other requirement.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 42(1)–(3); CRA Articles 2 and 12

blocks: Article 42(3) points to the **Cyber Resilience Act**, or CRA. Its scope and Article 12(1) conditions must be met: product cybersecurity requirements, relevant manufacturer vulnerability-handling processes and declaration evidence. That bridge deems the AI Act cybersecurity requirement satisfied; it is not full AI Act conformity.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 42(1)–(3); CRA Articles 2 and 12

blocks: CRA Article 12(2)–(3) preserves particular assessment interactions and important/critical-product procedure rules. Read those conditions before choosing a route. The specified medical-device products are excluded by CRA Article 2(2), so Harbour's medical case does not automatically receive this CRA bridge. Current version and CRA application dates require a real-release lookup.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 42(1)–(3); CRA Articles 2 and 12
